newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close up slightly, small caps rally.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close up slightly, small caps rally.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chips ended moderately higher, but investors' focus shifted to small-capitalised stocks once again.
The benchmark Composite Index ended the day 1.59 points up at 1,158.42, while the Second Board index rallied to close at 619.40, up 14.44 points or 2.39 percent.
Volume was high, with 289 million shares traded, valued at 2.59 billion ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 332 to 230.
Khong Guan and Sriwani were among the most actively-traded stocks, up 10 and five cents respectively to 24.90 and 6.20 ringgit.
"There has been a mixture of institutional and retail activity in the market today," said a local institutional dealer at a bank-backed securities house.

"Foreign institutions are treating the news of the 600 million ringgit trade surplus for August with caution, while the September inflation figure of 3.6 percent is being ignored by the market," he added.
The dealer said that foreign institutions had been selectively buying blue-chip stocks.
Tenaga was up 15 cents at 9.45 ringgit on a slight rebound after Wednesday's selling pressure.
"The KLSE is on a 20-week uptrend at the moment," said the dealer.
"Any selling pressure there has been has been absorbed very well by the market," said another institutional dealer. "The market is on an uptrend," he added.

Dealers pointed to selective, futures-linked index buying of Tenaga, Maybank, Rashid Hussain and Malaysian Airlines as being contributory factors to the Composite Index moving up only slightly, even though main board volume was high.
Maybank was up 10 cents at 25 ringgit, Rashid Hussain was up 30 cents at 15.80 and Malaysian Airlines was unchanged at 6.90.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot October contract was up three points at 1,159.0 with 279 lots traded, and the November contract was up 4.4 points at 1,163.4 with 33 lots traded.
